messages:
support-jess: FYI incoming from RetailX — p95 looks fine but p99 jumped from ~450ms to ~1.6s after last deploy. They see dashboard p99 higher than raw histogram panel. Can someone triage?
observability-bot: alert: kernel.p99_latency > 1.2s (service=api-infer) — fired at 2338001235
alicia: thanks Jess. Can you paste the dashboard panel query + the raw histogram query? also which model/route?
support-jess: route=/v1/generate, model=rw-medium-1, dashboard uses our rollup metric (rollup:latency_p99) and the histogram panel is a histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
mike: common mismatch: rollup is derived from downstream summary of per-host p99s, histogram uses aggregated buckets which can skew the tail. But a 4x jump is big. Any traffic spike or retries from gateway?
sam: also check sample weighting. If a few hosts started logging higher counts due to a retry storm, the aggregated histogram will push tail up depending on bucketization. can you run a quick raw sample query? e.g.:
```
curl -s "http://prom:9090/api/v1/query_range?query=histogram_quantile(0.99,sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))&start=...&end=...&step=60"
```
support-jess: running now, attaching graph link: https://graf/redwood/q/retailx-p99-spike (customer-facing)
nisha: RetailX says spike aligns with a batch job they started at ~14:05 UTC that hit /v1/generate in parallel. Could be queueing/backpressure on a few instances.
alicia: ok two diagnostic steps: 1) compare per-host p99s (sum by instance) vs rollup p99s 2) inspect the histogram bucket counts around >1s to see if mass moved into a higher bucket. Run:
```
# per-host p99 via quantile_over_time on histograms
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (instance, le))
```
mike: FYI we rolled in a kernel optimization in last deploy that changed internal timer rounding for the async executor. It could shift some long tails if we changed how KV cache causes backpressure. I'm rolling a canary to the previous runtime patch now.
sam: small gotcha: Prometheus histogram_quantile interpolates between buckets; if buckets were rebinned (we recently changed bucket boundaries from 100ms,200ms,... to 125ms,250ms...), the quantile can move unexpectedly. Check metric metadata for bucket le labels before/after deploy.
support-jess: metadata check: buckets changed on 2338001100 during deploy - le labels updated. this might explain mismatch. customer upset, asking for mitigation.
alicia: mitigation options (short-term): 1) temporary fallback to previous deploy on a small subset of hosts to see if p99 reverts 2) enable our legacy rollup mode which computes percentiles from raw samples (less efficient but exact) 3) advise customer to stagger their batch job.
nisha: I'll propose a stagger to RetailX while eng confirms. We need a repro to the support ticket though.
sam: repro steps for eng: 1) simulate parallel batch hitting /v1/generate at 100 RPS across 10 hosts with same model 2) capture per-host request_duration_seconds_bucket before/after the deploy variant 3) run histogram_quantile and our rollup pipeline to compare numbers. I can push a k6 script if helpful.
alicia: please attach k6 and the exact prometheus queries to the ticket. If the rebin is root cause, long-term fix: keep bucket boundaries stable or add a rebin-compatible transform in the rollup job.
mike: quick rollback on canary started at 2338001250. monitoring for p99 drop.
observability-bot: deploy: canary rollback initiated by mike at 2338001250
support-jess: RetailX confirms p99 dropped back to ~480ms after canary rollback. They've asked for a postmortem and an explanation for dashboard discrepancy.
alicia: Great — that'll prove the change caused it. Next steps: create a postmortem, include diff of bucket le labels, provide recommended mitigation (stable buckets + rollup fallback + customer guidance). I'll own the postmortem.
sam: will add a short grafana notebook showing interpolation effect with sample synthetic histograms.
nisha: I'll update the customer and include ETA for postmortem. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
